background: Citigroup is the holding company of the most international of the large US banks, with services, markets, banking, wealth and US personal banking as its main lines, and a multi-year restructuring behind it.
synthesis: All three of the main agencies rate the group, A- on average and BBB+ at the weakest of them, one on a positive outlook and two on stable, with no rating action since a one-notch downgrade by one of the three on 2 Dec 2015. Capital is on the weak side of US banks, CET1 of 11.8% and leverage of 5.2% both below the peer median, with leverage down 0.4 points since 30 Sep 2025 and CET1 broadly flat. Liquidity is the stronger leg, LCR of 128% in the top quarter and up 11 points since 31 Mar 2024 (figures to 30 Jun 2026). Flagged items in the last 90 days run both ways: an improved outlook reported on 27 Sep 2026 against a UK penalty for sanctions-control failures at a group unit earlier in the month, a conduct cost and not a threat to the balance sheet.
